# dsh-papercut
**Papercut explainer films, end to end — natively on Windows, no WSL.**

A DeepSeek Harness plugin that turns one sentence of
idea into a finished vertical (9:16) cut-paper

explainer: script → local text-to-speech →
word-level timed captions → Remotion render → QA contact

er: script → local text-to-speech →
word-level timed captions → Remotion render → QA contact sheets.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Why this exists

The upstream papercut-explainer library is a
beautiful Remotion kit, but its toolchain is 27 bash an

d Python scripts written for macOS
(Apple `rsync`, `mlx-whisper`, Homebrew `ffmpeg`, `readlink -f`).

Everything that touches the
OS has been rewritten here in Node, so the whole pipeline runs on a sto

uches the
OS has been rewritten here in Node, so the whole pipeline runs on a stock Windows machine:
| Piece | Upstream | Here |
| Choreography | `render.py` + `render.sh` | `src/node/render.js` — one bundle, per-scene ProRes HQ

segments, content-keyed cache |
| Audio mix | `mix.py` (numpy) | ffmpeg `sidechaincompress` + `alimi

ter` + `loudnorm` |
| Voice | `narrate.py` (qwen-tts) | local IndexTTS-2.5 bridge over HTTP |
| Word
timing | `asr.py` (mlx-whisper) | `openai-whisper` + forced alignment against the known script (`py

/align.py`) |
| Chromium | system Chrome | the Edge that ships with Windows |
| ffmpeg/ffprobe | `br
ew install` | bundled static binaries from npm |

No WSL. No Homebrew. No `ffmpeg` on `PATH`. Python is only needed for two leaf scripts
(forced align
ment, CJK font subsetting), and the plugin calls the interpreter you point it at.
## The six tools
| Tool | Arguments | What it does |
| `papercut_list` | — | Existing episodes, their duration, scene count and whether a render exists |
| `papercut_plan` | `idea`, `slug?`, `comp?`, `lines?` | Scaffolds the episode and returns the 7-li

ne script brief |
| `papercut_storyboard` | `slug` | Camera / cut / SFX table derived from the real

frame plan |
| `papercut_voice` | `slug`, `engine?`, `force?`, `model?`, `keepWarm?` | Local TTS per

line, silence trim, forced word alignment, `voiceover.wav` + captions + plan |
| `papercut_render`
| `slug`, `force?`, `workers?`, `conc?` | Segmented Remotion render, then one x264 pass with the aud

io bed |
| `papercut_qa` | `slug`, `every?`, `scale?` | Contact sheets every N frames, numbered, for
rcut_qa` | `slug`, `every?`, `scale?` | Contact sheets every N frames, numbered, for visual review |

Everything else — composing scenes, writing the hook, choosing assets — is the agent's job,
guided b

e — composing scenes, writing the hook, choosing assets — is the agent's job,
guided by nine skills.
## The nine skills
Installed into `<DSH_HOME>/skills` by `npm run skills`, so DSH picks them up live:

`papercut-explainer` (router / end-to-end) · `papercut-strategy` · `papercut-hook` ·
`papercut-scrip

t` · `papercut-storyboard` · `papercut-build` · `papercut-voice` ·
`papercut-qa` · `papercut-setup`
(toolchain doctor for this machine).
Say "make a papercut reel about X" and the router takes it from there.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## What the workspace must look like

`dsh-papercut` drives a *workspace* directory holding the upstream library and the render app.
The p

lugin finds it by walking up from its own package folder (and then from the current working
director

y) looking for `app/node_modules` + `src/papercut-explainer-main/library`, so a linked
checkout and

an npm-installed copy both work without configuration. Point it elsewhere with
`root` in `cordis.pat
ch.yml`, or the `PAPERCUT_ROOT` env var.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Use `papercut-setup` (or `node tools/bin/papercut.mjs list`) to see what is missing.
## Requirements

- **Windows 10/11** with Edge (any modern Edge has the headless Chromium Remotion needs)
- **Node 22

+**
- A Python 3.11 virtualenv with `openai-whisper` + `fonttools` — only for the aligner and
the CJ

K font subsetter. Point at it with `python:` in the plugin config.
- **Optional**: a local TTS HTTP

bridge on `127.0.0.1:7865` (IndexTTS-2.5). The plugin probes
`/health` and tells you how to start it

; it never spawns the model itself, because that would
hold VRAM hostage.

## Verified numbers
First film, `episodes/01-jianzhi` (1080×1920, 30 fps, 824 frames):

| Voice + alignment | 7 lines, 24.1 s of speech, ~4 s synth + ~3.3 s align per line |
| Render (cold

) | 55 s — bundle 2 s, 824 frames in 3 parallel workers, final encode 9 s |
| Render (one scene chan

ged) | 20 s — cache hits on the other six segments |
| Output | H.264 High, yuv420p, bt709, 8.6 Mbps
, −14.7 LUFS, −1.0 dBTP, 0 decode errors |
